reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern exhibits a robust, approximately 83-point periodic structure composed of repeating step-like plateaus punctuated by sharp, narrow negative spikes (troughs) and occasional broader positive ramps. Each cycle typically contains one dominant negative spike of amplitude ~0.7–1.0 (robust standardized units), often preceded or followed by smaller oscillatory wiggles (~0.2–0.5 amplitude). Plateaus are relatively flat (slope near zero), but mild monotonic trends (±0.004 per point) appear across longer windows; these are consistent with difference-stationary behavior and do not indicate drift. Amplitude envelope is stable: 90th-percentile amplitude ranges 1.44–1.78, with MAD varying 0.40–0.69 due to local noise density, not structural change. Peaks are rare and shallow (<0.3); troughs are sharper and more reproducible in timing and depth. Noise manifests as high-frequency micro-oscillations (2–5 points wide) clustered around troughs or transitions, especially in candidates 1–3. Boundary truncation is minimal; all candidates show full cycles without abrupt cutoffs. Acceptable variation includes: (i) slight differences in spike count per cycle (1–2), (ii) minor plateau height shifts (±0.1), (iii) presence/absence of secondary micro-spikes, and (iv) small trend offsets over 3–5 cycles. The core motif—sharp negative spike embedded in a stepwise baseline—is highly conserved.

reference_profiles.description: Single-cycle (83 pts) excerpt showing clean, isolated negative spike near index 8–10, followed by a deep trough (~−0.75), then gradual recovery. Plateaus are very flat; no micro-oscillations. Minimal noise; appears ‘idealized’ but lacks the richer spike clustering seen elsewhere.

Three-cycle window with higher noise density: multiple small negative spikes (2–3 per cycle) and visible micro-oscillations around troughs. One strong positive ramp (~1.0) near mid-window. Slight positive trend (slope +0.0013). More representative of typical operational variability.

Three-cycle window similar to candidate 1 but with slightly stronger negative spikes and a gentle negative trend (slope −0.0043). Micro-oscillations present but less dense. Trough depths reach ~−1.0; plateaus slightly less flat than candidate 0. Shows natural variation in spike morphology.

Five-cycle window revealing long-term curvature (curvature 0.35) and consistent spike repetition. Contains the most micro-oscillations and secondary peaks. Plateaus show subtle undulations; one cycle has a double-spike structure. Best captures multi-cycle stability and acceptable morphological diversity.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer candidate 3 for queries with ≥3 cycles or ambiguous trend/curvature; its length and morphological richness make it most robust to variation. Use candidate 1 for short queries (1–2 cycles) with moderate noise and clear spikes. Candidate 2 is optimal when a gentle negative trend is present. Candidate 0 serves only as a clean template for spike shape verification—avoid if query shows any micro-oscillations or multiple spikes per cycle.
uncertainties: Exact spike timing jitter (±2–3 points) across cycles is unquantified but visually consistent
Whether micro-oscillations are intrinsic dynamics or measurement noise remains ambiguous
